prompt: Pick a project size and see which providers actually fit:

options.label: Small personal project
options.content: A DigitalOcean droplet, Railway, or Fly.io is the right call. You get one box (or one small service), a bill you can predict exactly, and you can have something live in an afternoon. You will never touch a fraction of what AWS/Azure/GCP offer here — which is exactly the point. Paying for that depth would mean paying in setup time and console complexity, not just money.

options.label: Enterprise system
options.content: This is where AWS/Azure/GCP earn their complexity: fine-grained IAM permissions, compliance certifications, multi-region failover, audit logging, and the ability to provision thousands of servers on demand. A droplet-style provider has no equivalent to reach for when you need those — you'd be building it yourself. The console being intimidating is the cost of that depth actually being there when you need it.
